subject: RFI response: model catalog provenance & redistribution governance
messages:
From: Alyssa Chang <alyssa.chang@starkindustries.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RFI: Model catalog, licensing & provenance — follow-up

Marcus / Neha —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Procurement and legal at Stark are collecting written responses for the RFI. Could you provide a short technical + legal response that covers the following points by end of day Thursday (Dec 10):

1) Which open-source licenses do you ingest and surface in the model catalog (examples: MIT, Apache-2.0, GPL variants)? Do you re-license any upstream weights when delivering through Redwood?
2) What provenance metadata do you maintain for each catalog entry (model card, training dataset summary, upstream checkpoints, checksums, model_id/version)? Is that metadata machine-readable and exportable?
3) How does version pinning work for customers in production? Can we pin to an immutable artifact and who controls updates/rollbacks?
4) What is your process for notifying customers of model updates and behavioral changes (changelogs, semantic versioning, regression tests)?
5) Are you able to provide an SBOM or checksum manifest for model weights and their third-party components?
6) For redistribution / derivative commercial use: what language do you provide customers to include in their agreements to clarify rights and restrictions?

If you have a PDF or short packet that addresses these items, attach it. Also flag any follow-up items that require legal review.

Appreciate it,

Alyssa Chang
Senior Procurement Manager
Stark Industries
alyssa.chang@starkindustries.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chang <alyssa.chang@starkindustries.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: Model catalog, licensing & provenance — follow-up

Alyssa —

Thanks for the clear list. Attached is a concise RFI packet that addresses each item (see attachments). High level answers here; the attached PDF includes examples and machine-readable snippets.

- Licenses we surface: We ingest and surface upstream license metadata for all cataloged models. Common licenses we encounter and include in the catalog UI/metadata are MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-family, CC-BY (for certain weights), and select permissive academic licenses. We do not re-license upstream weights. For Redwood-owned published models, we include the explicit license in the model card (e.g., Redwood Public License v1.0).

- Provenance metadata: For every model entry we store a model_card (human-readable), a machine-readable provenance bundle (JSON-LD), upstream source URL, a list of upstream artifacts, training-data summary (high-level, non-sensitive), binary checksum (SHA256) for the artifact we serve, model_id (namespace:model_name:version) and an immutable artifact fingerprint (commit hash + build id). The attached model-provenance-schema.jsonld is the canonical format we export.

- Version pinning & immutable artifacts: Customers can pin to an immutable artifact ID (artifact fingerprint). Once pinned, the serving runtime will always resolve to that artifact unless the customer updates their pin. We support semantic channels (stable, beta, nightly) and recommend production workloads pin to explicit artifact fingerprints. Rollbacks are customer-controlled (re-pin) but Redwood provides one-click rollback tools and preserves older artifacts for reproducibility as part of the retention policy defined in the contract.

- Update notifications & regressions: We publish changelogs and a short behavioral-delta summary for each catalog update. For Redwood-managed hosted customers we send automated notices to the account contacts and (optionally) open a canary rollout for a pinned percentage. We run a standard set of regression evals for each major update; customers can choose to receive eval outputs and/or subscribe to a daily digest.

- SBOM / checksums: We provide a machine-readable manifest containing checksums for model weights and third-party components included in the served artifact. Where an upstream license prevents redistribution of the raw weights, the manifest still contains the checksum and source URL.

- Redistribution & derivative use: Redwood does not change upstream license obligations. We provide a suggested clause customers can insert into their vendor agreement to clarify that Redwood supplies metadata and delivery of artifacts under the upstream license and that customers are responsible for compliance when they redistribute or commercialize derivatives. For Redwood-licensed models we provide explicit grant language. See attached proposed-licensing-clause.txt for a starting point.

Next steps: 1) PDF + machine-readable bundle attached; 2) If you want specific clause language for Stark's procurement template, we can draft it with legal (it may take one business day); 3) Happy to do a 30-min sync if that helps.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Head of Product — Model Catalog
Redwood Inference
attachments: RFI_Response_Redwood_Model_Catalog_2026-12-08.pdf; model-provenance-schema.jsonld

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: RFI: model catalog provenance & redistribution governance — suggested edits

Marcus —

Quick suggested edits before we send the PDF to procurement/legal at Stark:

- Add a short paragraph about Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) and how customers can retain exclusive control of artifact storage and KMS-wrapped keys for checkpoint decryption. That usually resolves redistribution concerns for enterprise legal teams.
- Call out that for models imported under restrictive upstream terms we only surface a proxy artifact (serving-only) and provide the checksum + upstream access instructions rather than re-hosting.
- Mention retention windows for older artifacts and our default retention policy (90 days for hosted artifacts unless contractually extended).

I updated the proposed-licensing-clause.txt with a suggested sentence for KMS and private storage; please merge if you agree.

—Karthik
Lead, Platform Integrations

From: Alyssa Chang <alyssa.chang@starkindustries.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: model catalog provenance & redistribution governance — follow-ups

Thanks — this is very helpful. A couple clarifications before we route to legal: 

1) For redistribution/derivatives: can you provide explicit example language that covers (a) internal-only derivative models vs (b) commercial redistribution of derivatives (re-selling or embedding in a redistributable product)? We want to give legal drafts to our counsel rather than open-ended guidance.
2) For the machine-readable provenance: does the JSON-LD include the training-data provenance fields you referenced (high-level summary only) and a clear source_url + checksum for the exact artifact the customer downloads?
3) Is the retention policy for artifact storage negotiable under Dedicated / Private contracts?

Also — we prefer a short call to review the clause. Are you available for 30 minutes on Fri Dec 11 09:30-10:00 PT?

Best,
Alyssa

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chang <alyssa.chang@starkindustries.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: model catalog provenance & redistribution governance — call confirmed

Alyssa —

Thanks — confirmed for Fri Dec 11 at 09:30 PT. We will bring a draft clause that explicitly separates (a) internal-only derivative use (b) commercial redistribution of derivatives and (c) reseller scenarios. Short answers to your clarifications:

1) We will attach two precedent clause variants you can share with counsel (internal-use permissive text + commercial-redistribution language that includes attribution and upstream license obligations). See attached proposed-licensing-clause.txt.
2) Yes — the JSON-LD includes limited training-data provenance fields (dataset_id references, high-level description, non-sensitive counts) + source_url + SHA256 checksum for the artifact we provide. We include a manifest so customers can verify binary integrity.
3) Retention is negotiable — Dedicated and Private contracts commonly include extended retention and archiving terms; we will note that in the contract appendix.

Action items: 1) I've attached the three attachments referenced earlier; 2) we'll join the call with legal if you want; 3) Marcus to follow up with a redlined clause if Stark's counsel requests changes.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Head of Product — Model Catalog
Redwood Inference
attachments: proposed-licensing-clause.txt; RFI_Response_Redwood_Model_Catalog_2026-12-08.pdf; model-provenance-schema.jsonld
